correctness.rationale: The inverse h^{-1}(w)=sqrt(1+3w)-1 yields the displayed radical exactly. The derivative has a positive-coefficient factorization when c<=d, proving full pgf positivity and normalization through theta=2/5. The only singularities are the two roots of the numerator and denominator; their moduli cross uniquely at theta_* defined by the cubic. An inverse-square-root positive real singularity gives the explicit n^{-1/2} asymptotic including equality, while the competing numerator zeros contribute only n^{-3/2}. Above theta_* the conjugate complex simple-root branchpoints have smaller modulus and the positive point at that radius is regular: Pringsheim applied to both eventual signs forces infinitely many positive and negative coefficients. The theta=1 isolated identity is excluded; exact rational checks are supplemental, not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The September 2026 full-text construction (Example 7) and December 2024 Example 6.5 both explicitly exhibit only 0<theta<=1/4 for the same zero-truncated-binomial two-trial conjugacy. The present 0<theta<=2/5 coefficient positivity is proved by a new nonnegative radical factorization; the algebraic cubic/eventual-sign phase is not stated there. Published published-finding corpus dispersion research quantifies moments after admissibility, not the admissible coefficient sign domain. Multiple targeted semantic searches and primary-section comparisons found no exact equivalent or stronger implication. Residual risk from algebraic combinatorics theory is acknowledged.
residual_risks: Published dispersion record was searchable but its complete linked repository text was not accessible. The available summary concerns a mathematically different moment problem.
A classical polynomial coefficient-positivity or branching-composition theorem could subsume this specific algebraic cutoff under nonobvious terminology.
The actual full pgf threshold in (2/5,theta_*] is unresolved and explicitly not part of the claim.

value.rationale: This model is the first nontrivial zero-truncated-binomial conjugacy singled out in the recent construction, where maximal admissible-parameter characterization is an explicit open direction. The result enlarges a rigorously admissible and composition-closed interval from 1/4 to 2/5, supplies a sharp algebraic threshold for eventual coefficient positivity, and reduces pgf membership below this threshold to finitely many coefficient obstructions for each fixed parameter. These are structural mathematical facts about parameter admissibility rather than a routine renaming or isolated numerical estimate. The exact full pgf boundary is intentionally left unresolved.
